minutes.headline: Water district found both main-replacement engineering bids too high and will seek other quotes and study pipe lining.
minutes.summary: Commissioners signed warrants, approved the July 21 minutes, and reviewed two engineering proposals for the water main replacement. The new attorneys rejected the Stantec agreement, and members objected to the prices, so they will get comparison proposals and information on lining the old main. They also covered the granite sign going to the planning board, the 40B project on Howard Street, a conservation staging area and loam screening, and a radio tower permit.

budget_items.what_was_said: Two proposals compared; the pricier one included a full-time on-site inspector, the cheaper dropped it.
Members objected to the cost of delineation and design for a roughly 3,000-foot main.
Money was appropriated at the annual meeting in March; material costs are said to have risen so the project may exceed it and the scope may shrink.
Lining an eight inch main was estimated at a cost comparable to replacement.

what_happened.line: The commissioners rejected the current engineering pricing for the water main replacement and will tell Stantec the board was unhappy.
They will gather information on pipe lining and request proposals from other engineering firms for comparison.
Two proposals were compared; the pricier included a full-time on-site inspector, and members objected to delineation and design costs for a main of roughly 3,000 feet.
The granite sign goes to the planning board on August 23rd for final approval.
The board discussed asking the ZBA to require escrow for long-term maintenance of a 40B pump station and tank, and informally agreed to consider renting a loam screener.

why_it_matters: The water main replacement was funded at the March annual meeting, and the minutes say material costs have risen, so the project may exceed that appropriation or its scope may shrink.
Pipe lining was estimated at a cost comparable to replacement, and the 40B escrow question bears on who pays long-term upkeep for the pump station and tank, which could reach water rates or taxes.
